title: Swe senior domain indexing strategies
question: Beyond just 'add an index on the column you filter on', how do you actually decide what indexes a table needs, and when would adding one hurt more than it helps?
idealAnswer:
Explains that a standard B-tree index speeds up equality and range lookups on the indexed column(s) but every additional index adds write overhead, since each insert/update/delete has to also update the index

Discusses composite (multi-column) indexes and column order mattering, an index on (a, b) efficiently serves queries filtering on a, or a and b, but not efficiently serves a query that filters on b alone

Identifies when an index won't help or is redundant, e.g. a column with very low cardinality (few distinct values, like a boolean), or an index that's a strict prefix of another existing composite index

Names a real cost of over-indexing beyond write latency, e.g. increased storage, longer index maintenance during bulk writes, and the query planner having more (sometimes worse) choices to consider

Mentions using actual query plans (e.g. EXPLAIN) to verify an index is being used as intended rather than assuming it helps just because it exists
